lbd.definition: the search for connections that no single document states but that follow from linking what separate documents say
lbd.excludes: finding links that some document already states, which is ordinary retrieval

link-prediction.definition: ranking pairs of nodes that are not yet joined in a network by how likely they are to become joined later
link-prediction.excludes: recovering links that exist but were hidden at random from the same snapshot

concept-link.definition: two concepts appearing in the same document; a concept here is a question tag on the Stack Exchange sites and a word or word pair on the research notes
concept-link.excludes: any judgement that the two concepts are related in fact

target-pair.definition: a pair of concepts never linked in the training slices that appears together in at least two documents of the next slice
target-pair.excludes: pairs that appear together only once in the test slice, and any check that the later pairing is true

time-slice.definition: one of five blocks of equal document count cut from a corpus ordered by date; a fold trains on the early slices and tests on the next one
time-slice.excludes: random splits, which let later documents inform the training graph

degree.definition: the number of other concepts a concept is linked to in the training graph, our measure of how popular it is
degree.excludes: how many documents mention the concept

abc-model.definition: scoring an unlinked pair A and C by the intermediate concepts B that each is linked to; here a cosine over shared neighbours with each edge weighted down when both of its ends are popular
abc-model.excludes: methods trained on known outcomes, and the expert reading that Swanson applied to each candidate

preferential-attachment.definition: a ranking of unlinked pairs by the product of the two concepts' degrees, so the most popular pairs come first
preferential-attachment.excludes: any use of which neighbours the two concepts share

adamic-adar.definition: a count of the neighbours two nodes share in which each shared neighbour is weighted by one over the logarithm of its own degree
adamic-adar.excludes: the popularity discount on edges that the A-B-C score uses

precision-at-k.definition: the share of a ranker's 200 highest-scored unlinked pairs that turn out to be targets
precision-at-k.excludes: how the ranker orders pairs below the top 200

base-rate.definition: the share of all unlinked candidate pairs that are targets, the precision a random ranking would reach on average
base-rate.excludes: the precision of any particular ranker

document-bootstrap.definition: redrawing the test slice's documents with replacement, recomputing which pairs are targets, and rescoring the fixed top-200 lists each time, so the interval shows how much the result depends on which documents happened to arrive
document-bootstrap.excludes: uncertainty from the training graph, which is held fixed

roc-auc.definition: the chance that a randomly chosen target scores above a randomly chosen non-target; 0.5 is chance and 1 is perfect
roc-auc.excludes: how the top of the list performs, which precision in the top 200 measures

stratified-auc.definition: the area under the ROC curve computed separately inside each tenth of the candidate pairs ranked by degree product, then averaged with weights equal to each tenth's number of targets
stratified-auc.excludes: any advantage that comes from ranking popular pairs above unpopular ones

degree-preserving-rewiring.field: network science, after Maslov and Sneppen
degree-preserving-rewiring.definition: repeatedly swapping the ends of two randomly chosen edges, so every concept keeps its degree while who is linked to whom is scrambled

node-permutation.definition: shuffling which concept sits at which node of the training graph, so the graph's shape stays and its link to the real concepts is broken
node-permutation.excludes: any change to the shape of the graph
